misclassified_entities.name: EVM Executor
misclassified_entities.reason: The EVM executor is an internal component of the Ethereum client. It triggers transaction begin/commit/rollback within the same process boundary. This is not an external entity but part of the internal state machine.
misclassified_entities.correct_classification: Internal EVM component - execution engine within the same process

misclassified_entities.name: Smart Contract
misclassified_entities.reason: Smart contracts executing SELFDESTRUCT are internal EVM execution context elements, not external entities. The contract code runs within the EVM, which is inside the system boundary.
misclassified_entities.correct_classification: Internal EVM component - contract bytecode executing within EVM

misclassified_entities.name: EVM Storage Opcodes
misclassified_entities.reason: SLOAD and SSTORE opcodes are internal EVM instructions, not external entities. They operate within the EVM execution context.
misclassified_entities.correct_classification: Internal EVM component - opcode execution within EVM

misclassified_entities.name: EVM Transient Opcodes
misclassified_entities.reason: TLOAD and TSTORE opcodes are internal EVM instructions for transient storage, not external entities.
misclassified_entities.correct_classification: Internal EVM component - opcode execution within EVM

misclassified_entities.name: Transaction Value Transfer
misclassified_entities.reason: Value transfer operations are internal state transitions triggered by transaction processing, not external entities.
misclassified_entities.correct_classification: Internal EVM component - transaction processing within EVM

coverage_analysis.note: All 5 listed external entities are misclassified as they represent internal EVM/state machine components, not true external entities outside the system boundary.

external_entities.name: Remote Peer Node
external_entities.rationale: P2P network peers exchanging ForkIDs during handshake are unauthenticated and may be malicious. Peers can send false ForkIDs to attempt to connect incompatible nodes.
external_entities.validation_required: ForkID must be validated against local chain configuration. Incompatible or stale peers must be rejected.

trust_boundary_edges.security_assumptions: Peer ForkID data is untrusted. Must validate FORK_HASH matches expected value for peer's claimed state. Reject stale or incompatible peers.

misclassified_entities.name: Chain Configuration
misclassified_entities.reason: Chain configuration is an internal trusted resource loaded at node startup from static files or compiled defaults. It is not an external entity sending data into the system at runtime.

external_entities.name: Decentralized Application
external_entities.rationale: Web applications requesting user signatures are untrusted. Dapps can be malicious or compromised, attempting to trick users into signing harmful data.
external_entities.validation_required: Typed data must be parsed and displayed clearly to user. Account address must be validated. User must explicitly approve before signing.

external_entities.name: Wallet User
external_entities.rationale: Human users are trusted to make authorization decisions but may be deceived by UI spoofing or social engineering. The user's approval decision is authoritative once made through authentic UI.
external_entities.validation_required: Wallet UI must clearly display data being signed to prevent user deception.

external_entities.name: Malicious Actor
external_entities.rationale: Explicitly modeled attacker attempting signature replay attacks. Must never be trusted.
external_entities.validation_required: Domain separator provides cross-contract/cross-chain replay protection. Applications must implement nonce-based replay protection.

external_entities.name: Verifying Smart Contract
external_entities.rationale: On-chain contracts verifying signatures could be malicious or contain bugs in verification logic. However, they are also recipients of the signed data rather than sources.
external_entities.validation_required: Contract must correctly implement EIP-712 verification. Application-level nonce tracking needed for replay protection.

trust_boundary_edges.security_assumptions: Dapp signing requests are untrusted. Typed data must be validated, parsed, and displayed to user for approval. Never auto-approve.

coverage_analysis.note: EXT-USER interacts via UI approval buttons without data-carrying edges. EXT-ATTACKER and EXT-VERIFYING-CONTRACT are modeled for security analysis but don't have direct inbound data edges in the signing flow.

external_entities.name: Peer Node
external_entities.rationale: Network peers propagating blocks are unauthenticated and may send invalid blocks or blocks from forked chains.
external_entities.validation_required: Blocks must be validated against fork rules based on network and block number.

coverage_analysis.note: EXT-PEER-NODE is defined but has no explicit edge in the subgraphs showing data flowing into the system. Block reception is implicit in the validation flow.

external_entities.name: Block Producer
external_entities.rationale: Block producers (validators/proposers) creating blocks with blob transactions are not trusted to follow rules. Blocks must be validated against blob count and gas limits.
external_entities.validation_required: Blob count must be <= MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA (9). Blob gas must be <= MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK (1,179,648).

coverage_analysis.note: EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER is defined but has no explicit inbound data edge. Block production and reception is implicit in the validation flow.
